checks.label: Twelve screens: five that show and seven puzzles, alternating to the ninth and ending on three mixed puzzles

Isolating circuits one at a time until the reading recovers: with any healthy feeder open the monitor still reads 0 kΩ; with F6 open it recovers to 3,000 ÷ 7 = 429 kΩ, above the 100 × 440 = 44 kΩ alarm line
The fault can disappear because the faulty load is switched off: with the pump stopped the monitor reads 3,000 ÷ 8 = 375 kΩ, and 429 kΩ with healthy F3 open, its lamp out
At 60 Hz: 440 ÷ 1.732 = 254 V and ω = 377 give 96 mA a line for each µF, 287 mA once the hull shifts; F1 reads 575 mA, each short feeder 14.4 mA, F6 661 mA
The earth current of a short faulty feeder is hard to tell from that of a long capacitive feeder: faulty F6 reads only 86 mA more than healthy F1
The test pulse flows via the live conductors, the fault and earth back to the device: F6, the sub-board incoming and Pump read 10 mA, every other clamp 0 mA
With the fault off the system (the pump stopped, or F6 open), every clamp reads 0 mA at 60 Hz and with the pulse, and no pulse path is drawn
With the solid fault on F1 instead, F1 reads the other seven feeders' 7 × 0.05 = 0.35 µF a line × 287 = 101 mA, and each short feeder 14.4 mA
Insulation resistance is measured at a DC voltage of at least 500 V: at 500 V the whole circuit and the motor read 0.00 MΩ, the cable over 200 MΩ, with the pump circuit off the system
Partial faults, from paths in parallel: 20 kΩ beside seven 3 MΩ feeders reads 19.1 kΩ, 19.2 kΩ with F3 open; 15 kΩ beside four 1 MΩ feeders (250 kΩ) reads 14.2 kΩ, beside three (333 kΩ) 14.4 kΩ
Before an answer, no puzzle's picture shows its result
The dead-test sorter takes only the right order: isolate, prove dead, disconnect the electronics, test, then split
Each demonstration settles within 5 s of its screen opening, and opening F6 lifts the needle past the alarm line within 1 s
